# Paging and virtual memory

## Virtual memory

Virtual memory gives each process its own address space that is independent of physical memory. The operating system divides the address space into fixed-size blocks called pages. Physical memory is divided into blocks of the same size called frames. A page table maps each page of a process to a frame.

## Page faults

A page fault occurs when a process accesses a page that is not currently in physical memory. The operating system then loads the page from disk, which is much slower than reading memory. If too many page faults occur, the system spends most of its time swapping pages, a condition called thrashing. A translation lookaside buffer caches recent page table entries to speed up address translation.
